transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-01-28 15:00 UTC
Duration: 34 minutes
Attendees: Sana Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Wu (Redwood SE), Maya Thompson (Neptune CTO), Alex Rivera (Neptune ML Eng)

Summary: Quick discovery focused on self-serve onboarding, free credits, and how fast Neptune can get first tokens. Customer is leaning PLG with eventual Dedicated or Private for production.

00:00 - Sana: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, yeah this is Sana from Redwood, and Ethan our SE is here as well. How are you all?
00:12 - Maya: Hi Sana, doing well, thanks. Appreciate you fitting us in, we've been poking around the quickstart.
00:20 - Alex: Hey, Alex here, quick intro: I'm the ML eng working on our recommendation model, looking at inference infra.
00:30 - Ethan: Great, yeah quick agenda — we want to understand your current stack, latency/cost goals, and whether self-serve hosted will work or you'll need Dedicated/VPC. Also we'll show how to get first token quickly.
00:45 - Maya: Sounds good, we're on GCP, using Vertex for training and a mix of in-house endpoints for inference. Main goal is to reduce latency at 99th pct and cost per inference, but also strict data governance — some PII flows in logs.
01:05 - Sana: Got it. Can you say more about QPS and payloads? 
01:10 - Alex: Typical payloads are 250-600 tokens, avg 320, peak 80 QPS for A/B tests, long term maybe 200QPS. Latency target is sub-200ms p50, p99 ideally <350ms.
01:28 - Ethan: Good, those are useful numbers. For quickstart, self-serve Hosted API gives you immediate access — free credits to spike and validate time-to-first-token in minutes. Dedicated is best for predictable throughput and SLAs, Private/VPC if you need customer-managed networking and KMS.
01:48 - Maya: About the free credits — what does that include? Is there a time limit? Any restrictions on model sizes?
01:55 - Sana: We give trial credits on sign-up, typically enough to run a week of exploratory tests. No hard model-size restriction on Hosted, but huge long-running workloads you'd move to Dedicated. Free credits expire after 30 days. Also we can grant more for pilot projects.
02:12 - Alex: Nice. Time-to-first-token — what's the typical flow for a dev? SDK or curl?
02:18 - Ethan: You can do curl in under five minutes. Our SDKs (Python/Node) give a one-line client, then call generate or chat endpoint. If you stream, you can see token-level streaming in real time. We can demo a quick snippet after.
02:35 - Sana: We also have a Quickstart template for recommender trials — it includes batching guidance and a preconfigured prompt set.
02:44 - Maya: On security: we're SOC 2 type 2 and need our vendors to be SOC2 as well, plus SSO/SAML and customer KMS integration for key management. How does Redwood handle those?
02:58 - Ethan: Redwood is SOC 2 compliant; we support SSO/SAML and RBAC. For encryption, hosted supports data-at-rest and in-transit; for customer-managed keys and VPC peering, that's available on Private deployments. Dedicated offers some KMS integrations depending on contract. I will follow up with our security pack.
03:18 - Maya: Great, can you send the SOC2 report and an excerpt of network flow controls?
03:23 - Sana: Yes — action: we'll send SOC2 docs and a short network architecture note.
03:28 - Alex: Performance — any published benchmarks for p99 latency on hosted GPUs? We saw some results on your site but wanted specifics for 320-token payloads.
03:37 - Ethan: Our public benchmarks show p50/p90/p99 for several models. For your payloads, we recommend a mid-sized open model quantized for throughput or a hosted high-perf variant. For 320 tokens at ~80QPS, Dedicated gives predictable p99; hosted sometimes has more variance but is usually fine for spikes. We'll share a benchmark sheet and can run a bespoke test with your sample prompts.
04:02 - Maya: If we do a pilot on Hosted, will results map to Dedicated later? Concern about mismatch when we move to dedicated hardware.
04:12 - Sana: Good question. We try to keep model variants consistent — same model family with different runtime optimizations. We provide performance profiles and recommended quantization so you can predict differences. Also we offer assistance during migration to Dedicated to tune kernels and batching.
04:28 - Alex: About data retention — logs and prompts, can we opt out of logging? We need to avoid storing PII.
04:36 - Ethan: On Hosted we have options to disable logging and purge data after X days; for full control you go Private where logs never leave your VPC. We'll include the exact retention config in the security doc.
04:50 - Maya: Ok. Cost — how should we think about tokens vs per-request costs? Our team is sensitive to per-inference unit economics.
04:58 - Sana: Primary is per-token billing for generation/embeddings; Dedicated is negotiated (monthly commit) which lowers unit cost. Optimize with batching and prefix caching; our Optimize tool gives suggestions on batching size and quantization to hit cost targets.
05:14 - Alex: Can you explain prefix/KV caching? We've tried local caches but KV cache for long sessions is new to us.
05:21 - Ethan: KV cache is the model's key-value attention cache — we persist and reuse it for repeated contexts to avoid recomputing. For recommendation use cases where context repeats, it dramatically reduces per-token compute and latency. Redwood handles cache affinity and eviction policies in the serving runtime.
05:40 - Maya: Nice. For the quick PoC, we want to validate latency and quality. What's a realistic pilot scope?
05:47 - Sana: Many customers do a 2-week pilot: 1) onboard devs on Hosted quickstart, 2) run a 2-3 workload benchmarks and quality evals with your prompts, 3) collect metrics and then decide Dedicated or Private. We can extend credits and support.
06:02 - Alex: That fits. SDKs — which languages, and are there code samples for streaming?
06:08 - Ethan: Python, Node, and a curl reference. Streaming sample included in the repo. We'll drop a link in the follow up.
06:16 - (crosstalk)
06:20 - Sana: Quick demo offer: if you're up for it we can spin a short live quickstart now — but I don't want to take time if you'd prefer to do it offline.
06:27 - Maya: We can do offline, just want the data to share with infra team first.
06:33 - Sana: Understood. One thing to note — time-to-first-token for a dev is often under 10 minutes: sign up, confirm email, get API key, run curl or SDK. If you need SSO-enabled onboarding, it can take a bit longer but we'll help.
06:50 - Alex: Any friction with service limits on Hosted? Limits on concurrent connections?
06:56 - Ethan: We have默认 limits for new accounts (rate limits) but for pilots we lift them. Dedicated gives you guaranteed capacity.
07:04 - Maya: Governance — audit logs and traceability for requests?
07:09 - Ethan: Console provides per-token cost and request trace, and we emit traces that can be routed to your observability stack. For Private, logs stay in your environment.
07:22 - Maya: If we wanted to start with Hosted for devs and then Dedicated for production, typical timeline?
07:28 - Sana: From pilot to Dedicated can be anywhere 4-8 weeks depending on procurement and infra. For some customers it's faster if they pre-commit.
07:36 - Alex: Procurement — do you require long-term commitments for Dedicated?
07:40 - Sana: Typically monthly or annual reserved capacity contracts; there is flexibility. We'll include draft terms.
07:48 - Maya: Ok. Can you run a small latency benchmark with our sample prompts? We can upload dataset to S3 and share access.
07:56 - Ethan: Yes, please share sample prompt set and a small corpus; we'll run it against hosted and provide numbers. If you want Dedicated simulations, we'll approximate using our Dedicated pool.
08:06 - Maya: Security contact — I'll share our security lead's email so you can coordinate SOC2 exchanges.
08:12 - Sana: Perfect. We'll send a short packet: SOC2, SSO config, retention options, and the network architecture doc.
08:20 - Alex: For Private deployments, what's the typical footprint? Do you ship a VM image, or is it a managed appliance?
08:27 - Ethan: Private can be offered as a VPC-managed control plane or an on-prem package. On-prem is a containerized deployment with customer-managed networking and KMS. We'll provide details in the technical deep dive.
08:42 - Maya: Any customers in regulated healthcare or finance doing this?
08:46 - Sana: Yes, a few customers in healthcare use Private with HSM/KMS integrations and strict audit logs. We can share anonymized case studies.
08:55 - Alex: About model versions and rollouts: do you support pinned model versions and canary rollouts?
09:00 - Ethan: Yes—rollouts, canarying, and automatic fallback policies are supported in the Console. We also integrate evals so you can run regression checks on prompts before switching.
09:12 - Maya: Great. Pricing expectations — can you ballpark cost for 200QPS sustained on Dedicated?
09:19 - Sana: Ballpark wide range; depends on model and quantization. We'll avoid a hard number on the call; we'll send a Dedicated SKU example with committed throughput pricing.
09:30 - Alex: Understood. For the benchmark, can you also measure cost per request and token?
09:36 - Ethan: Yep we'll include cost breakdowns and token accounting.
09:41 - (brief silence)
09:45 - Maya: Anything else we should know about quickstart that helps our infra team?
09:50 - Sana: Quickstart repo has a minimal Docker dev container, sample prompt set, and a small harness to hit the API with streaming. It also contains a guide for moving from Hosted to Dedicated. We'll send the link.
10:05 - Alex: Great. On the technical deep dive, we want to include our infra and security folks — maybe schedule the deeper session next Tue?
10:13 - Sana: Works for us; we'll propose slots.
10:18 - Maya: Ok, thanks.

(--- Recap and next steps ---)
10:25 - Sana: Recap — action items: we'll send SOC2, network note, quickstart link, and pricing SKUs. Ethan will run an initial benchmark once you share the prompt set. We'll schedule the technical deep dive next week.
10:40 - Maya: That works. Thanks everyone.
10:45 - Alex: Thanks, bye.
10:48 - Ethan: Bye.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-typed proper nouns ('Readwood' instead of Redwood in auto transcript), some overlapping talk condensed.

References/Links mentioned: Quickstart repo link (sent in follow-up), benchmark spreadsheet (to be shared), SOC2 packet (to be shared).
